reports.text: Indication: new-onset seizure, SLE. Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium. Findings: no acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No hemorrhage. No mass or abnormal enhancement. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No white matter lesions. No vascular malformation; normal flow voids. Pituitary and orbits unremarkable.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 12/29/2023, arrival 15:05 by ambulance.

CC: seizure.
HPI: 34-year-old woman with SLE, Crohn's disease and HHT. Per boyfriend, she had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home, then was confused. He says that over the past several months she has complained of headaches and fatigue, and a red rash on her face has flared when she is in the sun. No prior seizures. No head trauma.
Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.

Vitals: T 37.8 C (100.0 F), BP 135/85, HR 88.
Exam: postictal, rouses to voice and follows commands. Erythematous rash across both malar areas and the nasal bridge. Oral mucosa without ulcers. Neuro: moves all extremities symmetrically, no focal deficit. Tongue without laceration.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 3.8, platelets 95 K. Creatinine 1.1. UA: protein 2+, RBC 5-10/hpf. ANA positive. Anti-dsDNA positive. C3 low, C4 low.

Assessment: new-onset generalized seizure in active SLE with cytopenias and low complements - concern for neuropsychiatric lupus. Admitted to medicine with neurology and rheumatology consults.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Medicine. Admitted 12/29/2023, discharged 01/02/2024.

Principal diagnosis: neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus presenting with generalized tonic-clonic seizure.
Secondary: SLE with leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and hypocomplementemia; Crohn's disease with rectovaginal fistula (seton); hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia; mild intermittent asthma; anemia.

Course: Neurology and rheumatology consulted. MRI brain with and without contrast normal. Routine EEG: normal background, no epileptiform discharges. No further seizures. Treated with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days, then prednisone 40 mg daily. Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily started. Headache resolved. Rash improving.

Discharge medications:
- levetiracetam 500 mg PO BID (NEW)
- prednisone 40 mg PO daily, decrease by 5 mg each week to 10 mg daily (CHANGED)
- hydroxychloroquine 200 mg PO daily
- mesalamine 1.2 g PO TID
- albuterol HFA PRN
- ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; rheumatology 01/16/2024; neurology 3 months. No driving per state law. Return for any seizure.

documents.title: Rheumatology post-hospital letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology - visit 01/16/2024.
Seen after admission for neuropsychiatric lupus with seizure. No further events. Prednisone now 35 mg on taper. Malar rash nearly resolved. No arthritis. Plan: complete taper to 10 mg; continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; levetiracetam per neurology. CBC and CMP in February through primary care, please forward. Return 3 months.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Multiple bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum normal.

Transabdominal and transvaginal. Uterus enlarged. Heterogeneous, markedly vascular endometrial tissue measuring 2.4 cm. No gestational sac or intrauterine pregnancy. Ovaries normal in size bilaterally. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged uterus with 2.4 cm heterogeneous vascular endometrial tissue; no pregnancy. In this setting consistent with gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Six pulmonary nodules in both lungs, the largest 1.4 cm in the right lower lobe. No pulmonary embolism. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Six bilateral pulmonary nodules, largest 1.4 cm, consistent with metastases in the clinical setting.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 06/08/2024, 19:45.

CC: shortness of breath, vaginal bleeding.
HPI: 34-year-old woman with Crohn's, SLE (neuropsychiatric lupus with seizure 12/2023) and HHT, recent rectovaginal fistula with seton. Two weeks of shortness of breath and irregular vaginal bleeding, heavier than her periods. Miscarriage at 10 weeks gestation followed by D&C three months ago.
Meds: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 130/85, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air, afebrile.
Exam: mildly tachypneic. Diffuse rales both lungs. Abdomen soft; uterus palpably enlarged.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 250. Serum beta-hCG 225,000 mIU/mL.
CXR: multiple bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.

Assessment: markedly elevated hCG three months after a pregnancy loss with an enlarged uterus and lung infiltrates - gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with pulmonary metastases until proven otherwise. Gynecologic oncology consulted; admitted.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology discharge summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Gynecologic Oncology. Admitted 06/08/2024, discharged 06/13/2024.

Diagnosis: choriocarcinoma (post-abortal gestational trophoblastic neoplasia) metastatic to lung. FIGO stage III. WHO/FIGO prognostic score 7 (high risk): antecedent abortion, hCG >100,000, more than four lung metastases.

Workup: pelvic ultrasound - enlarged uterus with 2.4 cm heterogeneous vascular endometrial tissue, no pregnancy. CT chest - six bilateral nodules, largest 1.4 cm. MRI brain - no metastasis. Tissue biopsy not pursued (hemorrhage risk; diagnosis on clinical and hCG criteria).

Treatment: EMA/CO (etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D / cyclophosphamide, vincristine) cycle 1 started 06/12/2024 with folinic acid rescue; tolerated. Oxygen weaned to room air by 06/11.

Discharge medications: home medications unchanged (mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, levetiracetam 500 mg BID, albuterol, ferrous sulfate).

Follow-up: cancer center infusion every 2 weeks; weekly hCG. Avoid pregnancy; reliable contraception. Primary care: routine.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology progress letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Visit 07/16/2024.
Cycle 3 of EMA/CO given. hCG falling appropriately: 225,000 at presentation, 8,420 on 07/09. Breathing normal. Fatigue as expected; no neutropenic fever. Continue EMA/CO every 2 weeks with weekly hCG; consolidation for three cycles after the first normal value.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology progress letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body: Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. hCG 212 on 08/06 and 4 on 09/03 (normal <5). First normal value reached. Plan three consolidation cycles of EMA/CO, last expected mid-October, then monthly hCG surveillance for 12 months. Tolerating treatment.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology end-of-treatment letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Visit 10/22/2024.
Completed EMA/CO, final consolidation cycle 10/15/2024. hCG normal since 09/03. Complete remission.
Surveillance: monthly hCG for 12 months. Pregnancy should be avoided for 12 months after completion of chemotherapy so that hCG can be followed; contraception reviewed with patient and partner. Return to work when energy allows. We will send hCG results periodically.
